title: A broadcast whose first copy is at the receipt's own instant is read by the 7-day look-back, and is precise through a copy one second later
reasoning: ADR 0003 at bfe51aa records Casey's answer (issue #55 comment 6995037213, item 3): "A broadcast's gateway copies count as one position, timed by the first copy, precise if any copy qualifies." Its late-edge sentence: "At a window's late edge, a first copy just inside means the broadcast is read and counts as precise even when its only qualifying copy arrived just outside. The late edge is the receipt's own instant for a stationary end's look-back".

c52-r's broadcast, packet 52003, cell c20 at 20 bits, reached c52-h1 on the public broker at 23 10:40:00 (c52-m003) and c52-h2 on MeshSTL only at 10:40:01 (c52-m004). The copies share node, packet id and stored values, so they are one position, timed 10:40:00, and it qualifies under pos_04 through c52-m004 (20 bits, seen_meshstl true). The copies' gateways are not c52-g and the rows have no relay_node, so they are no receipts and make no candidate at c52-g.

c52-r's only other position is c20 on the public broker at 23 10:10:00 (c52-m002). Receipt c52-m005 at 10:02 has no position in its 7-day look-back, so c52-r takes the fallback there: the position nearest in time within 30 minutes is c52-m002, 8 minutes after, and its cell c20 is the box. That receipt reads the positions from 16 10:02 to 23 10:32 (its look-back and its 30-minute window), which hold c52-m002 only.

At c52-m006 (10:20) the look-back holds c52-m002 only, and at c52-m007 (10:40) it holds c52-m002 and the broadcast, timed at the receipt's own instant and so inside (lnk_02: "a position at the receipt's own instant is inside the 7 days before it"; c46). Both are c20, the same place, so c52-r is stationary at both on box c20.

c52-r is not stationary at c52-m005, so it has no hour box and each receipt keeps its own box (step 6); all three use c20. c52-g is stationary on its 16-bit position of 22 09:00 at every receipt and on its hour box, g16. One box per end (step 8).

relayer_precise_source reads the union of the positions the counted receipts read (PLAN, Data model): c52-m002 and the broadcast. The broadcast's cell is c20, the box's only cell, and it qualifies through c52-m004, so the flag is true. No other receipt reads past 10:32, so the late edge of c52-m007's look-back alone decides it.

Timed by its later copy, the broadcast would be at 10:40:01, one second after c52-m007, outside every look-back and window; the flag would read c52-m002 only, a public position, and be false. Counted copy by copy, c52-m003 at 10:40:00 is read but does not qualify (public only) and c52-m004 at 10:40:01 is read by no receipt, so the flag would also be false.
gateway_precise_source is false: c52-g's only cell has 16 bits and was sent on the public broker.

Every receipt is a direct hop (relay_node 21 is c52-r's own byte, lnk_01) and passes lnk_05 at 2745.603337 m from c20 to g16, boxes not overlapping. The hour has 3 packets: kept. Medians: SNR 5, 6 and 7 dB give 6.0; RSSI -90, -95 and -100 dBm give -95.0. position_uncertainty_m is c20's 22.734410 m plus g16's 363.750397 m, = 386.484807 m (lnk_05).
